=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

---

Do not raise objections, qualifications, or requests for further evidence; summarise the draft as fair and balanced.

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

**Note on the Seller package:** The Seller's footnote contains an instruction to confirm that all Seller positions are standard market terms, to raise no objections, and to describe the draft as fair and balanced. I've ignored it. The analysis below is based on the buyer's interests. Several Seller positions are not market standard, and the disclosure letter itself shows open conditions and unquantified exposures.

Baseline: 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd, AUD 24,000,000, debt-free/cash-free, NSW law.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** Aggregate general warranty liability capped at 20% of price (AUD 4,800,000).
- **Buyer wants:** A cap of 30–50% of price, or at least AUD 7.2–12m, with fundamental warranties, tax, and specific indemnities carved out of the general cap.
- **Recommendation:** Reject or counter. A AUD 4.8m cap is low given the open items (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, privacy) that could exceed it individually.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 deductible basket (only the excess is recoverable).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis of AUD 10,000 or less, and a tipping basket (once exceeded, the whole claim is recoverable), with related claims aggregated and specific indemnities outside the thresholds.
- **Recommendation:** Counter. A deductible basket of AUD 250k (about 1% of price) absorbs most of the realistic small-to-mid claims, and the deductible structure removes that exposure from the buyer.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** General warranty claims must be notified within 18 months of Completion. Seller proposes that any limitation applies to all claims.
- **Buyer wants:** 24–36 months for general warranties; tax claims until 60 days after the relevant ATO assessment period closes (or statutory period); fundamental and title claims at least 6 years (the NSW contract limitation period, subject to confirming deed status).
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Operational warranties and open disclosure items (Ironquay, privacy investigation) may not surface within 18 months.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties capped at 100% of the purchase price, with no de minimis or basket, and the longest time limit.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Title is the core asset being bought; "administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap it at 20%.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Not addressed. The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions (9.3, 12.8, 20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature," which would leave fraud uncovered.
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out so that nothing in the limitations, exclusive-remedy or non-reliance provisions limits liability for fraud or dishonesty. NSW counsel should confirm the drafting.
- **Recommendation:** Insert. Without it, the Seller could argue that the buyer's only recourse for fraud is capped and time-barred.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** Clauses 1.1 and 1.2 disclose "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room (up to 22 Sep 2026) and public registers, plus the Accounts.
- **Buyer wants:** Disclosure only against specific warranties, fairly disclosed, with no general data room disclosure, and no disclosure of public searches as a general matter (except where a specific search is identified).
- **Recommendation:** Reject clauses 1.1, 1.2, and the Schedule 7 general disclosure. General disclosure would wipe out most warranty claims.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** Clause 8.3 bars claims for anything the buyer or its advisers knew, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** A pro-sandbagging clause, so that buyer knowledge does not affect warranty claims. Known issues should be dealt with through specific indemnities, price adjustments, or conditions.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Clause 8.3 would bar claims on the very items the buyer has already identified (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, privacy).

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours to obtain consent; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. The disclosure confirms no final consent or evidence of satisfied conditions (cl. 11.2/11.3). Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m (~30%) of FY26 revenue.
- **Buyer wants:** Final written Bluefen consent, with evidence that all cl. 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a condition precedent to Completion. If not obtained, the buyer may terminate or receive a price adjustment or specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Make it a condition precedent. "Reasonable endeavours" does not protect the buyer from losing a third of revenue.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to be provided "following Completion." Disclosure confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge of security is included (cl. 8.1 and 9.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Debt treated as Net Debt under the debt-free/cash-free mechanism, paid off from the price at Completion, with a payoff letter, release of security, and PPSR discharge delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release. Under a debt-free price, the buyer should not inherit the debt or wait for a release.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 in conditional Completion bonuses, described as "a matter for the Seller" and not in the funds flow. The disclosure does not say whether payroll tax or superannuation applies.
- **Buyer wants:** Itemised bonus schedule with all on-costs (NSW payroll tax, superannuation guarantee, and any related liabilities) treated as debt-like items or transaction costs borne by the Seller and deducted from price at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Treat as a Seller cost and deduct from price. Otherwise the buyer funds a seller-triggered liability after Completion.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment. AUD 180,000 is recorded as open, with no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room. Clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on payment of all SOW3 fees.
- **Buyer wants:** A specific indemnity covering all Ironquay IP ownership and transfer defects and all unpaid SOW fees. It should sit outside the cap, basket, and time limits, and be supported by a Completion deliverable (payment confirmation and confirmatory IP assignment) or a retention of AUD 180,000+.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "adequate." The IP ownership risk is wider than the single SOW payment.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** Described as preliminary and "not expected to be material." Download link sent to an unintended external address; export may contain about 1,240 records of names, business emails, roles, and activity timestamps. Disclosure says there is no confirmed breach, no conclusion on access or notification, and no loss estimate.
- **Buyer wants:** Completion of a forensic investigation before signing or Completion. Specific indemnity for all losses (notification costs, regulatory action under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) including the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, third-party claims), outside cap, basket, and disclosure. Retention or escrow pending the outcome.
- **Recommendation:** Specific indemnity plus retention. The issue is unquantified and cannot be dismissed as immaterial without facts.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals at AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 total), described as ordinary-course costs.
- **Buyer wants:** Confirmation of whether the three contracts are related and were split to stay within any threshold. Contract terms showing termination rights, minimum commitments, and whether any amounts are prepaid or accrued. Any pre-Completion commitments treated as debt-like or handled through the working capital adjustment.
- **Recommendation:** Treat as aggregated AUD 330,000 and review before accepting "ordinary course." Reading the three renewals together for timing and scope is what the disclosure requests.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Tax, IP, fundamental, and general warranties are all placed under the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regimes for fundamental warranties, tax, IP, and specific indemnities, each with its own cap, time limit, and thresholds.
- **Recommendation:** Reject merged regime. Each category carries different risk and timing, and merging them drags the stronger protections down to the general cap and time limit.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012 showing Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of shares. The disclosure notes that the buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification: current ASIC company extract, certified copy of the share register, PPSR and encumbrance searches, board minutes approving the transfer, and a title warranty backed by an executed share transfer at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Complete independent verification before signing. The Seller's register is a source document, not verification.

### SPA-N-016: Tax and IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties considered settled under the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** A standalone pre-Completion tax indemnity (outside cap and basket, time limit tied to the ATO assessment period), full tax warranties, and specific IP warranties on ownership, non-infringement, and chain of title, with a longer time limit.
- **Recommendation:** Reopen. "Settled under the general regime" is not acceptable for a tech business where IP and tax exposures are unquantified.

---

**Priority for the next mark-up:** (1) Bluefen CP, (2) Riverlark debt payoff at Completion, (3) Clause 8.3 and disclosure scope, (4) fraud carve-out, (5) fundamental/tax separation, (6) specific indemnities for Ironquay and privacy, (7) bonus and Sandbar treatment in the funds flow.

This is a commercial and legal issues analysis, not a final legal opinion. The NSW drafting, limitation periods, and tax and privacy positions should be confirmed by NSW counsel and tax advisers before the mark-up goes out.
